title: Boosting self hybridized exciton polaritons with metal clad WS2 waveguides
authors: Filip Majstorovic, Masoud Taleb, Victor DeManuel-Gonzalez, Kai Rossnagel, Nahid Talebi
abstract: The formation of Fabry Perot and guided wave self hybridized exciton polaritons in two dimensional materials results in long range exciton energy transfer and strong exciton exciton interactions. Here, we demonstrate that the coupling strength between photonic modes and excitons is significantly boosted by embedding the active excitonic layer in a metal clad WS2 waveguide. The photonic modes in this waveguide exhibit modified dispersion properties for both Fabry Perot type and guided wave exciton polaritons compared to pure WS2 flakes, and show an increased couplingr strength. Our results provide a robust approach for controlling exciton photon interactions and their coupling strength in hybrid heterostructures.
summary: The researchers demonstrate that embedding $	ext{WS}_2$ excitons within metal-clad waveguides ($	ext{Au}/	ext{WS}_2/	ext{Au}$) significantly boosts the coupling strength between excitons and guided photons. By combining theoretical modeling with momentum-resolved cathodoluminescence, they confirm enhanced polariton formation, offering a tunable platform for controlling light-matter interactions.
main_problem: The primary goal is boosting the coupling strength between excitons (in $	ext{WS}_2$) and guided photonic modes within metal-clad waveguides.
main_result: The gold cladding significantly enhances the exciton-photon coupling strength ($G$) to $190 	ext{ meV}$, demonstrating a robust method for controlling light-matter interactions in hybrid heterostructures.
method: The study combines theoretical modeling (solving Maxwell's equations) with experimental characterization using momentum-resolved cathodoluminescence ($	ext{CL}$) spectroscopy.
model_or_system: The system is an $	ext{Au}/	ext{WS}_2/	ext{Au}$ metal-clad waveguide. The physics is described by analyzing the formation of self-hybridized exciton polaritons, often modeled using a Hopfield Hamiltonian to quantify coupling strength ($G$).
key_observables: Momentum-resolved $	ext{CL}$ spectra showing anticrossing behavior, dispersion relations for lower and upper polariton branches, and calculated electric field profiles.
important_parameters: Coupling strength $G$ (up to $190 	ext{ meV}$), exciton energy ($	ext{A-exciton}$), guided mode resonance frequency, and waveguide thickness.
main_assumptions: The $	ext{CL}$ detection in the far field only captures radiatively outcoupled parts of the dispersion; the analysis relies on fitting polariton branches using established Hamiltonian models.
figures_summary: Figures show momentum-resolved CL spectra confirming resonances, calculated and measured full dispersion relations for varying thicknesses, and electric field profiles distinguishing mode confinement.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying initial resonances via $	ext{CL}$ spectroscopy to theoretically modeling the coupling using Hamiltonian approaches. It compares results from metal-clad vs. uncladded structures to quantify enhancement and discusses implications for slow polariton propagation.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it deals with engineered light-matter interaction in 2D materials, a core topic in quantum optics and open quantum systems research, particularly concerning cavity/waveguide QED effects.

Figure 3: Experimental angle-resolved cathodoluminescence spectra of Au/WS2/Au flakes with WS2 thicknesses of (a) 120 nm and (b) 130 nm, corresponding to the samples already shown in Figure 1. The maps are overlaid with fits to calculated branches arising from the interference of surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) and transition radiation (TR). The grey dashed line indicates the A-exciton energy at 1.97 eV. (c) Schematic side view of the sample and of the interference mechanism: SPPs are excited at the electron-beam impact position, propagate towards the flake edge, are scattered there into the far field, and interfere with transition radiation.
